clue.text: State official has opportunity to get list back

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance

indicators.note: back says the word for list is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: A government minister gets the chance to have a register returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal for the list; 'has' and 'to get' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancellor is a senior minister of state, such as Britain's finance minister.

clue.text: Dog food

explanation.surface: Something to feed the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, dog food, but it is two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A chow is a Chinese breed of dog; chow is also slang for grub.

clue.text: Stuffy, and the last of his line you say ?

indicators.note: you say means the word should be pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: a man who is the last of his family line has no one to inherit, so he is heirless

explanation.surface: A stuffy man who is the end of his family dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: HEIRLESS, with a silent H, is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room has no fresh air.

clue.text: City connected with some country market town

parts.note: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, England
a field is a piece of open country

explanation.surface: A city linked with a rural market town.
explanation.walkthrough: CHESTER is a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterfield is a market town in Derbyshire, England, known for its crooked spire.

clue.text: Disappoints, having told news badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of told news are put into a different, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone lets people down by breaking bad news clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone down is to fail them.

clue.text: Perhaps attack shift hours round north

indicators.note: round means the jumbled hours goes around the north
shift says the letters of hours are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A night shift working round the clock in the north may be under attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' and 'hours' together suggest a work period, but 'shift' is the anagram signal and 'round' puts the jumble around north.
explanation.definitionFit: An onrush is a forward surge, of which an attack is one example.

clue.text: Old story of a fuel return

indicators.note: return says the word for fuel comes back the other way

parts.note: gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: A tale from long ago about fuel coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns only the fuel; the a stays forwards at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long traditional narrative, originally a Norse or Icelandic tale of heroes.

clue.text: Opposed to profit, in a way

indicators.note: in places the profit inside the a and the way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
gain means profit

explanation.surface: Someone is somewhat opposed to making a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' looks like 'somewhat', but it is A and ST (street) holding GAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Against means in opposition to.

clue.text: Pervading feeling of hope, as term breaks up

indicators.note: breaks up says the letters of hope, as term fall apart and reform

explanation.surface: A general feeling of optimism as the school term ends.
explanation.walkthrough: A school term 'breaks up' when the holidays begin.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere of a place is its prevailing mood or tone.

clue.text: Maugham's play for Britishers of course ?

explanation.surface: A Somerset Maugham play described as being about the British.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition teases the British habit of thinking themselves superior: to a Briton, the British are naturally 'our betters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset Maugham wrote a 1917 comedy of this title; and the British, in their own eyes, are those who rank above everyone else.

clue.text: Leaves producer something in hand

explanation.surface: A plant that grows leaves, and an item held in the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition means part of the hand itself, not something held in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm tree bears great fronds; the inner surface of the hand is also so named.

clue.text: TV feature appears — on great RN characters

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first part above the second

parts.note: looks means appears

indicators.note: characters suggests the letters of great RN are taken as a set of letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A television programme seen on a big Royal Navy personality.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy; 'characters' rearranges GREAT RN into TRANGER under LOOKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Look Stranger was a BBC television documentary series.

clue.text: Hide stone ?

explanation.surface: Two terse words that look like an instruction to conceal a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' is a verb here: to pelt someone is to throw stones at them.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's skin with fur is a pelt; to bombard someone with missiles is also to pelt them.

clue.text: Allowances made for noble in Norfolk town

indicators.note: in places the noble inside the name of the Norfolk town

parts.note: Diss is a small market town in the English county of Norfolk
a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Concessions are granted to an aristocrat living in an East Anglian town.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England; 'in' puts the noble inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Discounts are reductions in price, things allowed off the full sum.

clue.text: What priest gave Jack to answer

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is another
a solution is an answer

explanation.surface: A priest gives Jack something in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (jack tar) and AB are both crossword sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is the forgiveness of sins pronounced by a priest after confession.

clue.text: Covered (with leaves perhaps) finest Wren structure

parts.note: the finest is the best

indicators.note: structure suggests the letters of the name Wren are built into a new shape

explanation.surface: An architect's finest building is strewn with foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wren' suggests Christopher Wren, the architect of St Paul's, but it is just four letters for 'structure' to rebuild.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestrewn means scattered over with things, such as fallen leaves.

clue.text: Someone's beginning the craft of drawing?

indicators.note: beginning picks just the opening letter of the word Someone's

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing craft

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone has started to learn the art of drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like art or skill, but it is a boat, the KETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing.

clue.text: Going in for collecting bank-notes, perhaps ?

definitions.text: Going in for collecting bank-notes, perhaps ?

parts.words: Going in for collecting bank-notes, perhaps ?
parts.note: reads as having a hobby of collecting banknotes, but means breaking in to take money from a bank

explanation.surface: A person takes up banknote collecting as a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going in for' is both taking up a pastime and literally entering a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking into premises to steal is housebreaking, and banknotes are typical loot.

clue.text: Appoint road-mender in the end

indicators.note: in the end says that the word in is placed at the finish
a mender fixes things, so the letters of road are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Name a man to repair the highway in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'road-mender' reads as a workman, but 'mender' is the anagram signal and 'in the end' places the word in last.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to appoint someone formally, especially to the priesthood.

clue.text: Titled woman gets appeal from bookmakers

explanation.surface: A noble lady receives a plea from betting shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as DO WAGER, a bookmaker's request to bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a titled widow holding her late husband's rank; 'do wager!' is a bookie urging punters to bet.

clue.text: Many an American book goes to the right client

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
US stands for American
a tome is a large book
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Lots of American books are sold to the right buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: C (100) is the crossword's 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer is a client of a shop or business.

clue.text: Old coin given me in Paris by artist

parts.note: moi is French for me
Gustave Doré was a French illustrator and artist

explanation.surface: A Parisian artist hands someone an antique coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A moidore was a Portuguese gold coin, once current in England.

clue.text: Italian resort appears a little grim, initially

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Italian holiday town at first seems a bit bleak.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'appears', but that is the link word joining definition to wordplay, so the definition is just 'Italian resort'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a seaside resort on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Reluctant to omit providing for heirs?

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to leave their heirs anything in their will.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as UN-WILLING: not making a will in favour of one's heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwilling means disinclined; read as not leaving a will, it describes failing to provide for heirs.

clue.text: Eager to collect a few old coins

indicators.note: to collect means the a and the coins gather the few between them

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for old British pennies, from Latin denarii
six, VI in Roman numerals, is a few

explanation.surface: A keen collector of a few ancient coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British pennies were written d; A and D surround VI (six).
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen or enthusiastic.

clue.text: A spirit arising from the river

indicators.note: arising in a down clue says the word for spirit reads upwards, in reverse

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A ghost rises up out of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a ghost, but it is the drink RUM, turned upwards by 'arising' to MUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amur is a long river forming part of the border between Russia and China.

clue.text: One has a shot at this villainous part

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a go is a shot or attempt, as in have a go

explanation.surface: An actor tries out for a role as a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a shot at' looks like one idiom, but it splits: 'One' is I, 'a shot' is A GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello, a famous stage role.

clue.text: Existing accommodation ?

parts.note: existing means living
room means space or accommodation

explanation.surface: A question about the lodging that already exists.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a definition: the room one lives in is accommodation for existing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A living room is the space in a home where the household spends its daytime.

clue.text: A mutiny of no note

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An uprising of no importance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nore mutiny of 1797 took place among Royal Navy ships at the Nore anchorage in the Thames estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1797 naval rebellion at that anchorage is known by its name.

clue.text: A drink or two holding Reg back

indicators.note: holding means the two drinks contain the next part between them

parts.note: the two drinks here are gin and beer
the second of the two drinks is beer

indicators.note: back says the name Reg is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink or two while holding Reg back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' gives two drinks, GIN and BEER, which hold GER, Reg reversed by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger beer is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with ginger.
